records.fullText: Memberships Resident Memberships Sterling Ranch residents can enjoy all the amazing amenities at the Overlook Clubhouse with their membership cards. There is no additional cost for club memberships for Sterling Ranch residents. It's easy to get your membership cards. Simply complete the Resident Amenity Form listing all family members and bring a copy of your closing documents to the Clubhouse. Each family member will receive a membership card to gain access to the clubhouse. Remember, a membership card (or a picture of the card) is required to enter the facility. Steps to Obtain Your Resident/Homeowner Membership Cards Once you close on your home in Sterling Ranch, complete the Resident Amenity Form . List each member of your household that lives in the house (including children). Memberships will not be given to family members not residing in the home. Proof of Sterling Ranch address will be required by all adults listed on the Resident Amenity Form that are 21 or older. Anyone 20 years of age or younger is not required proof of residency. Acceptable documentation includes closing documents, utility bills, driver's licenses, etc. You will receive a confirmation email when your membership cards are ready to be picked up from recreation@sterlingranchcab.com . Allow the Resident Services Team two business days to process your membership request and prepare your access cards. Replacement Cards Each resident requires a membership card (or a picture of your card) to access the Clubhouse. If you have lost your card, you may purchase a new one for $5.00. Guest Passes Each CAB Resident household receives 25 complimentary guest passes per calendar year. Each CAB Resident household is permitted up to two six (6) guests per day with an annual maximum of 25 guest passes per CAB Resident household. If the Clubhouse and pool are not at capacity, additional guests beyond six (6) will be permitted for a fee of $5.00 per guest. CAB Residents are encouraged to call and verify capacity before arrival. Additional guest passes may be purchased from CAB staff and should be requested at least 48 hours in advance. Guests MUST be accompanied by the CAB Resident, who always provides guest passes while using the Clubhouse and Pool facilities. If the resident does not accompany guests, they will be asked to leave. Non-Resident Memberships Non-resident memberships are available for $850.00, up to two persons per year. There are no prorations. records.fullText: Snow Removal Snow removal is a joint effort. Douglas County handles the public roadways throughout the community. The Community Authority Board (CAB) removes snow in common areas, trails, shared drives, and alley areas. Homeowners are responsible for snow removal from their sidewalks and driveways. CAB SNOW REMOVAL Snow removal is handled by priority when the accumulation reaches the required threshold for service. Priority 1- The Overlook Clubhouse, CAB offices parking lots. Priority 2- Shared Drives, Alleys, and Mail Kiosks Priority 3- Peripheral sidewalks, parks, and areas with streets but no homes. Ice melt/sand will be applied throughout the community in areas as needed for resident safety. Minimum Threshold for Service by Area Overlook Clubhouse - zero tolerance Sidewalks - 2" threshold Mail Kiosks - 2" threshold for priority removal. Shared Drives - 2" threshold Alley Areas - 4" threshold Regional Trails - 4" threshold *Motor Courts will only be serviced by the CAB with a single plow pass when Douglas County enters its Priority Tier 3 or when the community reaches a 7" trigger. Townhomes Please contact your HOA Management Company for service questions or issues. To Best Service These Areas: Trucks will use rubber blades in all shared driveway areas. Snow will be pushed to curb stops or pulled from drives when possible. Crews will use shovels to move snow over the curb stop when possible in an effort to keep the front entryways clear. Snow markers are installed in alleys and shared drives to create the broadest possible passing lanes. Snow Hauling from shared driveway cutouts will occur on a case-by-case basis depending upon the amount of snow piled. When a snowstorm is predicted, please help make snow plowing easier by: No parking in back-out areas at the end of the driveways. The back-out areas are designated as NO parking areas. Removing vehicles from shared driveways, alleys, and motor courts. Storing extended downspouts in the upright position. DOUGLAS COUNTY SNOW REMOVAL Douglas County is responsible for snow removal on all public roads. Douglas County clears all roadways according to priority until conditions are safe for travel. The County only provides a single, passable lane down the middle of each street. Cul-de-sacs and some local streets may not be plowed if accumulations are minor, and snow is expected to melt over the following 24 hours. Exceptions are made if the roads have hills or curves that may become icy and hazardous to traffic. For questions or concerns related to the areas of Douglas County, please use the contact information below. Douglas County Snow & Ice Removal Information Report Douglas County Snow and Ice Removal Concerns Douglas County Snow Priority Map Phone: 303-660-7400 DOUGLAS COUNTY SNOW REMOVAL ROUTE PRIORITY MAP Subd ivision street s are not plowed if parked vehicles or other obstructions interfere with the safe and continuous operation of snow removal equipmen t. When a snowstorm is in the forecast, residents are advised to move vehicles off the street if a snowstorm is forecast to allow safe access by snowplows. HOMEOWNER SNOW REMOVAL Snow and ice on sidewalks create a dangerous situation for all ages, especially for children, the elderly, and persons with disabilities who are more susceptible to injury. For these reasons, Douglas County Ordinance O-007-003 requires property owners in unincorporated Douglas County to remove snow and ice from the sidewalks adjacent to their property within 24 hours after it stops snowing. Direct all concerns on the homeowner responsible areas to Douglas County. Snow Placement Place all snow removed from sidewalks and driveways on your adjacent landscaped areas. This practice benefits the vegetation, reduces the amount of runoff, and helps manage the snow and ice in the street. Please do not place snow in the street. Doing so results in larger snow windrows in front of your home created by snowplows. Additionally, piles of snow in the gutter area interfere with drainage and result in buildups of ice in the gutter and on the sidewalk. Vehicle Placement When a snowstorm is predicted, remove your vehicle from the streets. During a winter storm, automobiles and other vehicles left parked on County streets, and roads make it difficult for snowplows to remove snow and ice. If you are in need of help shoveling, please email Kelsey at kstiltner@sterlingranchcab.com with your name and address. records.fullText: Community Volunteers Our community thrives because of the people who call Sterling Ranch home, and we’d love your help! From events and activities to special projects and community programs, there are plenty of ways to get involved. Whether you can give an hour here and there or take on a bigger role, your time and talents make a real difference. High school students can also earn credit toward their required volunteer hours for graduation. Ranch Hands Program Sometimes a little neighborly help makes all the difference! Our Ranch Hands pitch in to keep Sterling Ranch looking its best-whether it’s planting bulbs, raking leaves, or pulling those pesky weeds. Think of it as the summertime version of our Snow Angels program: instead of shovels, we bring out the rakes and gardening gloves to help those who cannot do this work themselves during a health crisis, family emergency, or other significant disruption in their life. Want to get your hands dirty (in the best way)? Sign up today and join the Ranch Hands team. Together, we’ll grow a community that’s not just connected, but rooted in kindness. Register here to volunteer as a Ranch Hand. Questions? We’re just an email away: info@sterlingranchcab.com Be a Snow Angel this Winter! When the snow starts piling up, some of our Sterling Ranch neighbors could use a little backup. That’s where our Snow Angels come in. These volunteers help clear sidewalks and driveways for those unable to shovel. It’s all about keeping our neighborhood safe, welcoming, and neighborly (and helping folks avoid slips, falls, or fines). Grab a shovel, spread some cheer, and be the reason someone smiles on a snowy day. Questions? Send us an email to get involved: info@sterlingranchcab.com Community Navigators Moving into Sterling Ranch is exciting-but it can also feel like a lot to take in. That’s where our Community Navigators come to the rescue! These friendly volunteers welcome new neighbors, extend a personal invitation to homeowner orientation meetings, and offer a warm smile and helpful tips to make settling in a little easier. Think of them as trail guides for life at Sterling Ranch-here to point you in the right direction and make sure no one rides the trail alone. Want to join the Navigators crew? Reach out to communitynavigators@sterlingranchcab.com Event Volunteers Looking for an easy way to get involved and meet your neighbors? Volunteering at a community event is a great place to start! We’re looking for residents to help out with short, flexible shifts-no experience or training required. We’ll provide all the details when you register, so you can simply show up, lend a hand, and enjoy being part of what makes our community special. records.fullText: NEW HOMEOWNER GUIDE W E L C O M E T O S T E R L I N G R A N C H Joy Resides Here -- 1 of 28 -- Welcome Home We're thrilled that you've decided to make Sterling Ranch your home! At Sterling Ranch, we value creating a sense of place and belonging. We embody the spirit of Colorado, the West, and Ranch Life values, such as respect for the land and the importance of community. As a master-planned community, we thoughtfully executed every aspect of our operations. Sterling Ranch is curated with plenty of open space, trails for walking and biking, and amenities that offer a wide range of activities and events for everyone. This New Homeowner Guide includes a wealth of resources to help you settle into your new home, and our team is always here to help. Sterling Ranch is a diverse, exciting group of people of all ages from across Colorado and the country. Our residents come together at events, activities, and volunteer opportunities to celebrate, make friendships, support each other, and have fun! We look forward to getting to know you and hope you embrace Ranch Life. Welcome home to Sterling Ranch. But here to help are Sterling Ranch’s community volunteer group, the Community Navigators. The Community Navigators are here to do exactly that - help new homeowners navigate the transition into life here in Sterling Ranch. While the Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board (CAB) is always here to help, outreach from other residents offers an informal and personal alternative. “As a new homeowner, I was so overwhelmed when I moved here several years ago,” says founding volunteer Kerri Buted, a resident of Prospect Village. “I thought, what if other residents could just call new homeowners and ask what we can help them with? We can answer questions or introduce them to other new residents. The idea is to help people start off with a positive experience.” Sterling Ranch averages 33 home sales each month, and volunteers divide the new residents among their villages; for example, new Prospect Village buyers are paired with established Prospect Village residents. “For those new residents, getting a friendly call from a neighbor can make a big difference and help them feel welcome,” explains Buted. The Navigators invite newcomers to the monthly New Homeowner Orientation meeting, which presents a wealth of valuable information, but can sometimes be overwhelming. After the initial phone call, the Navigators assist new neighbors in finding activities and clubs, and provide ongoing communication. “We are committed to welcoming and helping new homeowners,” says Buted. “I think the personal outreach is really making a difference.” One of our Community Navigators will reach out to you (if they haven’t already) to help you settle in. Or contact communitynavigators@sterlingranchcab.com for more information! 6 -- 6 of 28 -- Food Trucks to the Rescue! Every Evening from 4 - 8 pm at the Sterling Center You’re in the middle of moving. Boxes are everywhere, your new home is a flurry of activity and packing materials, and yet, the endless question remains… what’s for dinner? Never fear, rotating food trucks arrive in Sterling Ranch daily from 4 - 8 pm to serve up hot, delicious meals at the Sterling Center (8155 Piney River Ave.). Many new homeowners find this amenity to be a lifesaver (or at least a sanitysaver) during the first few weeks of moving. Food trucks at Sterling Ranch add convenience to our residents’ lifestyles long after the move-in period. From mouthwatering barbecue and authentic Greek food to creative East-meets-West fusions, a steady rotation of some of Colorado’s favorite food trucks satisfies our residents’ palates daily. Check out the food truck schedule on our website to see what tasty treats are coming each day. We also have a full schedule of engaging events on our calendar. Visit the Community Calendar on our website to stay up to date at: www.sterlingranchcab.com/calendar 7 -- 7 of 28 -- Technology at Sterling Ranch Intelligently Energizing Our Community and Homes We are the top-selling master-planned development in Colorado for several reasons, including our state-of-the-art smart home technology. Carbon Neutral Community By reducing our energy use and switching to clean, renewable energy supplies whenever possible, Sterling Ranch has minimized our impact on the environment. Some energy-saving steps include: Every home in Sterling Ranch is Energy Star compliant. Homes in Sterling Ranch come solar-ready. Garages come pre-wired for an electric vehicle charging station. Over 30% of the power supply comes from renewable energy sources. Intelligent streetlights dim at 10 pm and turn off at dawn, lowering energy usage and nighttime light pollution. Fiber Optic Network & High Speed Internet Our underground fiber optic network serves as the backbone of our community’s internet infrastructure. Our internet is already faster than average speeds across the nation, providing quick access to your information, communication, work connectivity or entertainment needs. 8 -- 8 of 28 -- Smart Homes Internet Lumiere is Sterling Ranch’s technology provider. Lumiere has partnered with Quantum Fiber to deliver internet service to your home. This program benefits residents by providing a modem, streamlined account setup, and dedicated customer service. Visit the Lumiere website for step-by-step instructions on setting up your new account, or schedule an appointment with Lumiere after closing on your new home: lumiere.technology/help or scan the QR code below. Smart Home Automation Systems For new builds, SmartThings is your all-in-one smart home automation system that comes standard in each new home and can be integrated with all your other smart home devices. For more about the SmartThings system and to download the phone app, go to the SmartThings Hub. For homes built prior to 2024, you will have the STEWARD Smart Home Automation System. Rachio Irrigation Controller Rachio uses local outdoor weather data to optimize your landscape watering patterns, giving your yard exactly what it needs. Copper Labs Energy Monitoring System and UtilityHawk Copper Labs is installed in every home in Sterling Ranch and provides nearly real-time feedback to residents regarding your electricity, gas, and water usage. The UtilityHawk app can alert you in case of a water leak. Need Help? Contact Lumiere to schedule an in-person technology consultation. They can help with additional services, upgrades, questions, and more. Scan the QR code below to get started! 9 -- 9 of 28 -- Trash Services New Homeowners Can Dispose of Extra Items for the First Month Your first month of pickups allows for an unlimited amount of trash on the day of your regular service. This allows you to dispose of moving boxes, packing materials, etc. After this grace period, trash and recycling must fit inside your containers; extra items will incur additional charges. Our trash company, Waste Connections (www.wasteconnections.com), utilizes automated trucks to service Sterling Ranch, providing an efficient experience for trash and recycling. Please review the following guidelines to ensure that trash is collected in a neat and organized manner. Trash Container Guidelines: Containers must be at the curb (not on the sidewalk or driveway) by 7 am on the day of service. NOTE: The area is home to various wildlife, including bears. Do not place trash out the night before. Containers should face the street with handles facing the house and wheels touching the curb. Please leave at least two feet of space between each container to allow for automated access. Do not park personal vehicles within 10 feet of containers on service day. Call Customer Service (303-288-2100) to schedule and prepay for large item pickups (i.e. furniture, carpet, wooden pallets, mattresses). Trash cannot be higher than the lid of the container or placed on top of the lid. Trash must be placed inside the container, not on the side. Do not place the following items in containers: Hazardous or prohibited waste materials, including motor oil, tires, batteries, herbicides, pesticides, and acid. Dead animals, dirt, sod, brick, concrete, rocks, construction material, wood, hot ashes, or flammable materials such as solvents, oil, gas, liquid paints, or medical waste. Trash Days: Providence Village: Mondays; recycling every other Monday. Ascent Village: Tuesdays; recycling every other Tuesday. Prospect Village and Parkvale: Thursdays; recycling every other Thursday. Extra Services: Large items are $20.00 per item. Call Waste Connections Customer Service at 303-288- 2100 to schedule and prepay for large item pickups, and to confirm allowable items. 10 Mattresses must be wrapped entirely in plastic. Large pieces of glass or mirrors must be put inside a taped box prior to pickup. Boxes must be flattened and tied together. Residents receive their water and sewer bills in the mail monthly and are billed in arrears. The Community Authority Board (CAB) uses a third party, AmCoBi, to administer the monthly water bill each month. The water rate billing structure includes a fixed monthly water service base fee and a residential usage charge. Rates and fees are established annually by the CAB Board of Directors. STEP 1: UNDERSTAND YOUR WATER BUDGET(S) Outdoor Water Usage Every home in Sterling Ranch with an irrigation system has a water budget for outdoor water usage. (If your home does not have its own irrigation system (townhomes will not have individual irrigation systems), please skip to the Indoor Water Usage section.) Homeowners should consider these water budgets when installing or changing landscaping to ensure landscape materials are appropriate for their budget. This three-month average becomes your indoor water budget for the rest of the year. The budget is recalculated annually during the same three-month time frame to accommodate changes in household size or habits. (New residents are assigned an initial water budget based on an estimated usage; this is customized as soon as you reside in the home during the three-month period from December through February.) STEP 2: UNDERSTANDING STERLING RANCH’S TIERED WATER RATE STRUCTURE Sterling Ranch uses a percentage-based tiered water billing system to promote conservation while ensuring fair and equitable costs for all households. Instead of a flat rate, this structure aligns water costs with actual consumption, encouraging responsible usage. How It Works · Water Budget Based on Your Needs: Each home has an indoor and outdoor water budget, as described in the first section. This customized water budget is based on household size and typical usage, ensuring basic water needs are billed at the lowest rate. · Tiered Rates: Water used within your budget is billed at the lowest rate (Tier 1). If usage exceeds your budget, the rate increases progressively based on how much over budget you are. As usage increases beyond this baseline, rates gradually increase in tiers. This means those who use significantly more water pay a higher rate for the excess, promoting responsible usage. · Fair & Conservation-Focused: The percentage-based tiers ensure fairness since every home’s indoor budget is unique, while also supporting long-term water resource sustainability. By using this approach, Sterling Ranch ensures that water remains accessible for essential needs while encouraging mindful consumption. records.fullText: All categories Home - FAQs Water Water Communication Retrofit Design Review Compliance Overlook Clubhouse Pool Frequently Asked Questions Overlook Clubhouse Pool 9 All Content What are the pool rules? All swimmers must check in at the front desk with their membership card or a photo of it. There is no pool entrance from the side gates. Children under the age of 11 years must be accompanied and actively supervised by a parent, guardian, or if authorized by a parent/guardian, another individual of 15 years of age or older, while using the Clubhouse or Pool. Swimming any time where a lifeguard is not on duty is at the swimmer's sole risk. Lifeguards may not be on duty when temperatures are below 65 degrees and inclement weather is present. All users must take a cleansing shower before entering the pool. Showering after using the pool is recommended. Appropriate swimwear must be worn at all times. Street clothing (basketball shorts, jean/denim materials, cargo shorts), undergarments, sports bras, or similar attire is prohibited in the pool. White t-shirts or tank-tops are permitted in the pool if worn over appropriate swim attire. Pool staff will make the final determination if swimwear is appropriate. Nudity is strictly prohibited. Non-swimmers must be accompanied by a swimmer in the water and be within an arm's reach at all times. Glass containers are prohibited in the pool and pool areas. Food and beverages are permitted on the pool deck. Food and beverages are not permitted in the pool. To avoid spilling food or beverages into the pool, please keep them at your chair or table. Users who are ill, have experienced vomiting or diarrhea in the past 24 hours, have open sores, or ear/nasal discharge should not use the pool. Swim diapers must be worn by all incontinent swimmers. Horseplay, running, diving into the pool, and hanging/swinging/pulling on aquatic equipment or features is prohibited. Repeat violators will be asked to leave the pool. Lane lines, stairs, and railings are installed to assist and guide pool users. Standing, hanging from, or sitting on these items is prohibited. When lap lanes are present, those areas are for lap swimming and water walking only. During busy times, lap swimmers may be asked to share lanes, circle swim, or limit swim time to ensure all have an opportunity to use the facilities. The pool deck is reserved for walking, safety, and emergency purposes. No obstruction of any kind will be permitted in this area. Inflatable pool toys, flotation aids, or similar items are only allowed under the following conditions: Only transparent, circular inflatables no larger than 42 inches in diameter, infant inflatables, water wings with an attached chest piece, and pool noodles are permitted in the pool. Mesh infant inflatables may be no larger than 33 inches by 38 inches. Pool mattresses or other inflatables are prohibited. Users with noncompliant inflatables or flotation devices will be asked to remove them from the pool. Personal sound equipment, such as stereos or wireless speakers, are permitted as long as they do not disrupt others' enjoyment of the pool. If any complaints are received, Users will be asked to turn down their music, use headphones, or upon repeated complaint, asked to turn off the device or leave the pool. The pool must be cleared during thunder and lightning storms or other inclement weather events that present danger to Users. The pool will be cleared if lightning strikes within 10 miles of the pool, or at the discretion of Clubhouse or Pool Staff. All users must follow staff directions and safety instructions. Staff will determine when it is safe to reopen the pool. Chemicals are used to ensure a sanitary and safe water environment. Conditions are tested and documented on a regular basis. If unacceptable conditions occur, including a vomiting or fecal event, staff will determine if the pool must be closed to preserve the health, safety, and well-being of all users. Chemicals used in the pool may damage swimwear. CAB is not responsible for any such damage. CAB furniture in the pool area shall not be removed. Users may bring additional, portable lounge chairs, umbrellas, or other similar items to the pool area, provided they do not present a safety concern or unreasonably interfere with others' use and enjoyment of the pool as determined by staff. Overlook Clubhouse Pool What are the hours of operation? Monday-Friday: 5:00 am - 7:00 am Lap Swim Tuesday & Thursday - 7:00 am - 8:45 am: Pool CLOSED for cleaning and maintenance. 9:00 am - 8:45 pm: Open Swim (Lifeguards on duty 9:00 am - 8:45 pm) School back in session: Lifeguard hours are 4:00 pm - 8:45 pm. Saturday: 9:00 am - 8:45 pm (Lifeguards on duty 9:00 am - 7:45 pm) Sunday: 9:00 am - 8:45 pm (Lifeguards on duty 9:00 am - 7:45 pm) Overlook Clubhouse Pool Will swim lessons be offered? Yes! The clubhouse lifeguard vendor will offer private swim lessons throughout the Summer. Each session days, times, and pricing will be coordinated directly through the vendor. Private swim lesson sign-ups will available on a first-come-first-served basis subject to instructor availability. Overlook Clubhouse Pool Can I bring a guest to the pool? Yes! Each household receives 25 guest passes each calendar year linked to your CIVICREC account. Each CAB Resident household is permitted up to six (6) guests per day. If the Clubhouse and Pool is not at capacity, additional guests beyond six (6) will be permitted for a fee of $5.00 per guest. CAB Residents are encouraged to call and verify capacity before arrival. Guests MUST be accompanied by the CAB Resident providing the guest passes at all times during their use of Clubhouse and Pool facilities. If guests are not accompanied by the resident, they will be asked to leave. When you arrive with your guests, please indicate the number of guest and we will deduct the passes from your account. Overlook Clubhouse Pool Can a caregiver take my kids to the pool? You can purchase a caregiver pass for $300.00 for the calendar year, listing up to four names to use the caregiver pass. ID will be required to use the pass and the individual must be with those they are giving care for. Only one person can use the caregiver pass at a time. Overlook Clubhouse Pool What is the capacity of the pool? 169 individuals are permitted at one time. Overlook Clubhouse Pool Will lap swim be available? Yes, each morning, Monday through Friday from 5:00a -7:00a is reserved for lap swim. We will also have at least one lap lane available during open swim times. Overlook Clubhouse Pool Can I reserve the pool for a party? Unfortunately, the pool is not available for rental. There are other great spaces at the Overlook to reserve for private parties! Overlook Clubhouse Pool Are reservations required? No. On April 16, 2021, Douglas County opted out of the Tri-County Health public order, thus allowing all businesses to operate at 100% capacity.
